sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: a denied request's audit log shows the violation reason, an egressViolations entry (request leaving the perimeter), the source project, the targetResource project and the principalEmail, with a vpcServiceControlsUniqueId to filter; the fix is an egress rule applied with --set-egress-policies whose egressFrom names the identities and whose egressTo names serviceName storage.googleapis.com, method selectors and the target project's resources; IAM is a separate check. The violation reason used in the case (RESOURCES_NOT_IN_SAME_SERVICE_PERIMETER) and dry-run behavior are from memory of the VPC Service Controls troubleshooting pages (to verify).

brief.situation: You are the security engineer at Northgate Clinical Research. Today the perimeter trials-perimeter, around project trials-data, moved from dry run to enforced. Tonight's export job, which writes a de-identified extract to the contract research partner's bucket in project cro-share (outside the perimeter), fails. The contract requires delivery by 22:00.
handover: The export runs as sa-export@trials-data; only it should write to cro-share, and only to bucket cro-share-inbound.
The dry-run logs for the last two weeks were never reviewed.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the perimeter around trials-data, the partner's project outside it and the export that crosses.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

egress.label: Add an egress rule: sa-export may call storage.objects.create on projects/cro-share only; apply to trials-perimeter
egress.available: not busy and (not fixed and not harmed)
egress.why: Already done, or the system is down.

effects.output:
secops@cloudshell:~$ cat egress-cro.yaml
- egressFrom: identities: [serviceAccount:sa-export@trials-data.iam.gserviceaccount.com]
  egressTo: operations: [serviceName: storage.googleapis.com, methodSelectors: [method: google.storage.objects.create]]
            resources: [projects/cro-share]
secops@cloudshell:~$ gcloud access-context-manager perimeters update trials-perimeter --set-egress-policies=egress-cro.yaml
secops@cloudshell:~$ gcloud run jobs execute export-cro

writeup.question: For the record: why the export failed after enforcement, what you allowed and how narrowly, and what happens before the next enforcement.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: The audit log showed an egress violation from trials-data to cro-share by sa-export: storage is restricted in trials-perimeter, enforced today, with no egress rule. The dry-run log had predicted it every night for two weeks.

parts.label: Allowed
parts.criteria: One identity, one method, one target.
parts.modelAnswer: An egress rule for sa-export, storage.objects.create, projects/cro-share. Removing the project from the perimeter would have opened the trial data to any IAM-authorized copy; more IAM changes nothing.

parts.label: Before enforcing
parts.modelAnswer: The remaining findings were reviewed with the data owner, and perimeters are enforced only after their dry-run log is resolved.

perimeterRemoved.headline: Open one door, not the walls
perimeterRemoved.body: VPC Service Controls exists to stop data leaving. A precise egress rule lets the one approved flow out and keeps everything else in.

deliveryMissed.headline: Perimeters are not IAM
deliveryMissed.body: A request must pass both IAM and the perimeter. The audit log's egress violation names what to allow in an egress rule.

egressRule.headline: Good: perimeter kept, flow allowed
egressRule.body: You read the violation, used the dry-run history, allowed exactly one identity, method and target, checked both the export and a blocked read, and made dry-run review part of enforcement.

scoring.modelReasoning: The audit log shows an egress violation: the approved export identity writing from inside the newly enforced perimeter to the partner's project outside it. IAM already allows it; the perimeter is a separate check. Add an egress rule for exactly that identity, method and target project, run the export, and confirm other flows stay blocked. Removing the project from the perimeter removes the protection; more IAM does nothing. Read dry-run logs before enforcing next time.
